metadata.title: Where the Galaxy Law Sets the Core: a0 and the Structure of Cold Dark Energy Halos, from Galaxies to Clusters (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 2.0 draft (2026-10-26). DRAFT ONLY, NOT DEPOSITED. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.

The owner's programme studies a galaxy law g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32 pi) (kappa = 1/2 fitted), and its covariant form v3s, on two a0 footings never pooled. The law passes SPARC, MeerKAT, isolated groups, tidal dwarfs, the screened Solar System and binary pulsars. Beyond galaxies it fails: cluster cores, faint dwarfs and the early universe require a cold, clumping component, called here cold dark energy: a gravitating w ~ 0 field component paired with dark energy, not matter and not a particle. Selectors, heating, feedback, early dark energy, recombination release and orbit-keyed conversion all fail, each with a named mechanism. The external-field test does not distinguish a fundamental law from one emergent from cold dark energy.

Core result: Burkert cores with rho0 r0 = a0/(2 pi G), no new constant, pass SPARC and the cluster outskirts but miss the heavy cores. The rule Sigma_core = max(a0/(2 pi G), eta Sigma_coll), eta = 14.83 from self-similar infall with an external formation concentration c_f = 4, passes SPARC and 14 of 15 cluster keys including the heavy cores, and fails two keys narrowly (groups, and the gas-richest clusters' outskirts). c_f is pinned by the data at about 4; scale-free infall and spherical peak collapse (post hoc, exploratory) both give 1.85 and fail. Collisionless zoom simulations in the record give a native c_f of 7.2 / 7.0 / 5.6 at 1e12 / 1e13 / 1e14 Msun, above the data window and not converged (uncertain by about a factor 2; more seeds are running). With the native c_f the rule passes SPARC, groups and every cluster key except the inner band of all 326 clusters, which it over-predicts (Z = -2.41): the closest result in the record with no borrowed number.

Below galaxies and the tether: the same a0-floor halos, with nothing new fitted, reproduce four of five Local Group dwarf classes and fail the Milky Way ultra-faints (under-predicted, Z +3.80 / +3.66). A local vacuum-set floor g_T = 0.254 a0 fails growth and self-consistency; a floor keyed on bound objects is consistent but nonlocal, and has no action. Current picture: a0 sets the cold dark energy core floor from dwarfs to large spirals; above galaxy scale collapse plus a native concentration sets the core. Open: the cluster inner band with c_f convergence, the ultra-faint halo masses, and an object-keyed tether mechanism.

An illustrative Cosmicflows-4 flow map with SPARC galaxies and nearby eRASS1 clusters is included; it is not evidence for the theory. No result here is evidence for the framework over LambdaCDM. Companion: PAPER60 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23601528). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).
